title: 御製律呂正義後編·卷三~卷四 (vol 4)
shelf_note: A Qing imperial treatise on court ritual music. The leaf is a woodblock-printed flute score of a sacrificial hymn. It sits plausibly in the general universallibrary collection.
structure_note: Only 4 of 149 records carry a printed number, so the 1 backstep and 1 repeat tell us almost nothing. They are most likely misread block-heart leaf numbers, not a splice. The structure count says pages_translated is 0 while the field says 124, so one of the two counters is wrong (E2). 129 of 149 pages have OCR.

pages.printed_marker: 律呂正義後編 (block-heart at the left edge, cut off by the frame; leaf number illegible)
pages.layout: woodblock score in eight vertical columns ruled apart, right to left; each large text character has a small scale-degree name and a small gongche fingering character beside it; rows of open circles in the lower half of each column; the heading 笛譜 has its own column

ocr_errors.image: several different small notation characters on the leaf (they look like 亿, 伬 and 仜, i.e. 乙/尺/工 with the person radical), e.g. 未羽亿, 歆角伬, 兮商仜
ocr_errors.problem: The OCR reads the gongche fingering characters as one glyph, 仉, and drops many of them (e.g. 禮羽亿 becomes "禮羽", 肴宮伬 becomes "宥宮"). For a flute score these characters are the notes, and that information is lost.

ocr_errors.image: a small notation character (looks like 伬 or 亿), e.g. after 洋羽 at the foot of the first column and in 行宮伬
ocr_errors.problem: Notation character misread as the word 俎 'sacrificial stand'
牷 'unblemished victim' misread as 牲 (so 牲 appears twice in a row)
几 'offering table' misread as 凡

ocr_errors.image: rows of open circles under the text in every column
ocr_errors.problem: The circle marks in the score are neither transcribed nor described

ocr_errors.image: woodblock print in a calligraphic style

tr_errors.problem: The OCR's conflated notation is carried over as romanised terms. 'kang' is not a reading of 仉 (zhǎng) nor of any of the notation characters on the leaf (yi, che, gong). The reader is given a fingering sequence the print does not have. The meta hedges this only as 'some pairings are uncertain'.

tr_errors.english: In the handwritten layout the fingering characters (伍, 仉, 俎) often stand on separate lines.
tr_errors.problem: The meta repeats the wrong 'handwritten' claim about a printed leaf

other.note: The meta and summary name the hymn "Han Ping" and its occasion (presenting the sacrificial stands, sacrifice to Earth). Neither appears on this leaf, and I cannot confirm them from it.

missing.why: Nothing in the reading text tells the reader that gong/shang/jue/zhi/yu are the five pentatonic scale degrees (only the summary says so), or that wu/kang/zu stand for flute fingering signs.

book_verdict: The hymn text and the scale-degree names are mostly read right, and the notes correctly flag three misread words. But the flute fingering characters, which are the substance of a score, are merged into one wrong glyph and romanised as an invented 'kang', so a reader cannot use this score.
